title.title: The hyperkähler SYZ conjecture, for every deformation type
title.subtitle: Claim: a nef isotropic line bundle on any hyperkähler manifold gives a Lagrangian fibration over $\mathbb{P}^n$

plain: Certain perfectly balanced shapes always split into a family of donut-like tori over ordinary projective space

panels.caption: the four known deformation types were done; the claim covers every type

lines.tex: L \text{ nef},\ q(c_1(L)) = 0 \;\Longrightarrow\; X \to B,\ \dim B = n

beats.text: Known type by type: $K3^{[n]}$, generalized Kummers, OG6 and OG10
Claimed for all: the fibration exists, and its base is always projective space

achievement.label: Hyperkähler SYZ conjecture; Matsushita's base question
achievement.context: Before: the four known deformation types; base $\mathbb{P}^n$ when it is smooth (Hwang, 2008)
achievement.note: With external boundedness: finitely many deformation types per dimension if $b_2 \ge 5$

verify.detail: No Lean; the two papers cite each other
verify.ourCheck: We graded the claim, not whether it is right

voice.text: Hyperkähler SYZ, for every deformation type.
On a hyperkähler manifold, a nef square-zero bundle should give a Lagrangian fibration.
Before, only the four known deformation types were done.
Claimed: every type, and the base is projective space.

sources.quote: every holomorphic line bundle L with nonzero nef isotropic class (q(c1(L))=0) is semiample, giving a Lagrangian fibration X → B with dim B = n
The base of every Lagrangian fibration of a compact IHS Kähler manifold is isomorphic to P^n
the finiteness corollary needs b2 ≥ 5 and the external EFGMS boundedness theorem. No Lean.
